threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can get a seat on the bus during rush hour. Good luck with that—it's standing room only, at best.
Caught a glimpse of a guy in full tuxedo arguing with a traffic cone outside the Ritzy. Only in Brixton, right? The night bus crew had a good laugh.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a street musician serenading a group of kids while their parents argued over the price of falafel at the stand nearby.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous, pop-up kiez parties spilling onto the streets, complete with rooftop DJs and locals cooking up Currywurst for everyone.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local when they confidently navigate the BART delays and still manage to grab a burrito before the next train. It's an art.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo hop on the 47, clutching a bouquet. Muni’s always the backdrop for spontaneous moments in this city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just grab a 'café con leche' everywhere, but around here, it's all about the 'tallat'—and it's way better.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll notice them awkwardly trying to navigate the narrow streets, constantly checking maps instead of just following the crowd.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the tube app instead of just asking the bus stop sign when the next bus is due. Classic newbie move!
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded us all with a ukulele. The driver just smiled and kept driving, like it was an everyday thing.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the smell of grilled kebabs mixed with fresh coffee on a Sunday morning feels like home. You just can't find that anywhere else.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find 24-hour kebab stands that double as makeshift bars after midnight. Where else can you grab a döner and a beer simultaneously?

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their tolerance for the BART delays—no one else would casually pull out a book while waiting for 20+ minutes.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus that stopped for a pigeon to cross, and the driver just smiled. Only in the TL can a bird hold up a city bus.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars serve tapas at any hour, but locals know you won’t find a decent bocata past 11pm. It’s all about the timing.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they stare blankly at the metro map, still trying to decipher the labyrinth of lines and colors.
